analysis.session_summary: The session was a pro-risk rotation: AUD led with +0.295% vs majors while USD lagged at -0.156%; SPX rose +0.958% and VIX fell -3.039%. Major FX ranges were narrow, with no leg owning its move; the only measured event reaction, US Unemployment Claims (203K vs 208K), was muted at 0.009% basket impulse. Commodity FX and gold outperformed while USD/CHF and USD/CAD slid -17.4 and -21.0 pips respectively. The tape is quiet and technically driven, leaving the coming Jackson Hole/Warsh window as the key catalyst.

themes.evidence: USD -0.156% vs majors, DXY -0.047%, USD/CHF -17.4 pips, USD/CAD -21.0 pips
Most zigzag legs carry confidence none; US Unemployment Claims 203K vs 208K produced only 0.009% USD basket impulse
Gold/USD +233.2 pips (+0.508%), AUD/USD +28.5 pips, NZD/USD +12.5 pips

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD alternated five legs (up 7.6, down -18.8, up 19.3, down -13.8, up 7.5) within a 23.2-pip day range, finishing only 2.4 pips higher with no leg owning its move.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY ran three legs (down -27.2, up 34.5, down -19.2) inside a 40.2-pip range, closing 12.4 pips lower as the BOJ Himino headlines failed to own any leg.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD chopped through five legs (up 6.4, down -10.0, up 8.1, down -20.9, up 19.1) in a 31.6-pip range, ending 3.1 pips higher with no clear driver.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF printed four legs (down -8.4, up 14.5, down -27.1, up 5.0) and closed 17.4 pips lower, with the largest leg owning no macro trigger.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD built higher in three legs (up 15.9, down -10.2, up 21.6) to finish 28.5 pips up at the top of a 33.9-pip range.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD swung from -5.3 to +18.7 to -35.8 to +1.9 over four legs, closing 21.0 pips lower near the low of a 38.1-pip range.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD posted four legs (up 14.3, down -17.2, up 17.4, down -3.4) and closed 12.5 pips higher, with no leg owning the move.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF slid 18.3 pips on the day after three legs (down -6.6, up 16.0, down -26.6), with the final leg lacking a clear catalyst.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY climbed 27.5 pips in a wide 87.3-pip range across five legs, with only one leg partially driven by BOJ Himino (+4.9, 20% share).
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD rebounded from an early 22.6-pip drop with two up legs (30.0, 30.5) to close 22.1 pips higher near the top of a 52.5-pip range.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP was confined to a 12.0-pip range, closing just 0.1 pips higher after seven small alternating legs.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF rose 10.2 pips on the day after an up leg of 24.8 pips was partly unwound by a -6.4-pip drift, with no clear trigger.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF finished just 0.3 pips lower in a 20.9-pip range, with five legs alternating and no leg owning the move.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR ran a 893.4-pip range in three legs (down -399.3, up 842.9, down -291.6), closing 28.1 pips higher with no clear catalyst.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN traded a 595.1-pip range in three legs (down -195.1, up 502.7, down -208.5), ending 65.4 pips higher with no leg owning the move.
leg_notes.Gold/USD: Gold/USD experienced three large legs (up 458.8, down -679.4, up 422.0) within a 765.8-pip range, closing 233.2 pips higher at 0.63 of range.
leg_notes.BTC/USD: BTC/USD rallied 2,389.9 pips on the day as three legs (up 2,362.1, down -1,244.5, up 1,146.6) left price at 0.86 of a 2,791.3-pip range.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent/USD was confined to a 274.8-pip range with four alternating legs (down -203.0, up 238.3, down -100.5, up 75.2), closing just -1.5 pips lower.

polarity_reads.read: Muted 0.009% USD basket impulse on a 203K vs 208K beat signals the market has already priced labor-market resilience; positioning is not short-dollar sensitive to second-tier data.

scenarios.name: Risk-on extension with Jackson Hole neutral
scenarios.thesis: Risk appetite holds after SPX +0.958% and VIX -3.039%, commodity FX leadership extends, and Warsh/Jackson Hole fail to produce hawkish repricing.
triggers: Jackson Hole delivers no hawkish surprise
scenarios.invalidation: USD rebounds if Warsh leans hawkish or benchmark payroll revision improves materially from -911K.

USD soft vs JPY; pair closed -12.4 within 40.2-pip range.

GBP/USD range is 31.6 pips; pair closed 3.1 pips higher, exposed to USD repricing.
USD/JPY range is 40.2 pips and closed -12.4; hawkish repricing can retrace higher.
